title: Composition and Expertise of Steering Committee for Singapore College of Islamic Studies
what_it_is: Composition and Expertise of Steering Committee for Singapore College of Islamic Studies

sections.label: Non-Muslim Board and Committee members
sections.summary: Non-Muslim members form less than half of the Board of Governors and Steering Committee and are appointed for their diverse expertise and experience with the Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The non-Muslim members make up less than half of the Board of Governors and Steering Committee, and are appointed for their diverse expertise and experience in working with the Muslim community.

sections.label: Board induction and community engagement
sections.summary: All Board members undergo a structured induction programme and regularly engage Muslim religious, community and madrasah leaders and students to understand how SCIS can best serve the community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: All Board members undergo a structured induction programme, which includes briefings on the mission, vision and values, and objectives of the College.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: They also engage regularly with Muslim religious and community leaders as well as madrasah leaders and students to understand how the SCIS can best serve the community.

sections.label: Student intake and career pathways
sections.summary: Questions were asked on expected yearly student admissions, planned graduate career pathways, and a dedicated professional development and career support unit, with plans for more than 50 students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, how many students does the Singapore College of Islamic Studies expect to admit each year?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, what are the planned career pathways for the graduates of this college?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And third, will this college have a dedicated professional development and career support unit for the students?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are planning perhaps for more than 50 students and we will expand this further.

sections.label: Advisory Panel members' feedback
sections.summary: Advisory Panel members said this is something they have been looking for, but no country has done it and their countries have different contexts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: When I engage the members of the Advisory Panel, they shared with me that this is something that they have been looking for, but no country has done it and in fact, their countries have different context from ours.

sections.label: Encouragement and MABIMS colleagues
sections.summary: The speaker is encouraged and also met MABIMS colleagues during a recent meeting.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, it is something that I am encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I also met my colleagues from MABIMS during my recent meeting.

sections.label: Engaging professionals for advisory roles
sections.summary: The speaker will look into engaging various professionals who can play advisory roles in planned efforts, including curriculum development and partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I will also look into how we want to engage the various professionals that can play a part.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will be looking at how they can even play advisory roles in some of the efforts that we plan, even some aspects of curriculum development and partnerships.
